reason: Re-opened packet.js quran 19 --verse 7.205: Ibn Kathir’s single comment on 7:205 to 7:206 opens with God commanding His remembrance at the start and end of the day, as He commanded worship at those two times (50:39), says this was before the five prayers were made obligatory on the night of the Isra and that the ayah is Meccan, and later, rejecting Ibn Jarir and Ibn Zayd (who tie it to listening to the Qur’an), says what is meant is urging the servants to much remembrance morning and evening lest they be heedless. The sentence carries exactly these: much remembrance at the day’s start and end, Meccan, before the five prayers. The ‘this was before’ could grammatically attach to the 50:39 command, but the standard reading (and the one that makes ‘this ayah is Meccan’ relevant) is of the ayah under comment; not drift. Range citation follows the voice rule. Plain sense matches day.js (7:204 heed the recited Qur’an; 7:205 to 7:206 close the surah). Pickthall’s ‘(O Muhammad)’ not relied on. verse.js ok (Al-A’raf 7:205), entry-check ok.
